shorts.title: What you will learn: C-style strings
shorts.hook: Old C strings still hide in modern code.
shorts.script: Old C strings still hide in modern code. Today we look at the old way to store text. C strings are everywhere, so you must know how they work. A C string is an array of chars. The last char is a special null character. It marks the end of the text. The null character has the code zero. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: C-style strings.

shorts.title: C-style strings in one minute
shorts.hook: A C string is an array of chars.
shorts.script: A C string is an array of chars. The last char is a special null character. It marks the end of the text. The null character has the code zero. The cstring header has helpers. Strlen counts the letters. Strcmp compares two strings. Think of a necklace of letter beads that ends with one blank bead. The compiler counts the letters and makes room for them. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: C-style strings in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: Two arrays hold the same text.
shorts.script: Two arrays hold the same text. Strcmp compares the letters. It returns zero when the texts are equal. So we test the answer against zero. The result is true, so cout prints one. The program prints one. A C string is a char array that ends with a null character. Strlen counts the letters. Sizeof counts all the bytes. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Comparing C strings with equals
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. Both arrays hold goa, but the test is never true. Two equals signs compare addresses, not letters. The compiler warns that comparing two arrays is deprecated. Use strcmp, or better, use std string. Two equals signs compare the addresses of the two arrays, not their letters. The addresses always differ. Use strcmp, or use std string. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Why did the C string feel empty? Its last bead was always null.
shorts.script: Why did the C string feel empty? Its last bead was always null. Write a loop that counts the letters of a char array, without strlen. Stop at the null character. Write your answer in the comments. A C string is a char array that ends with a null character. Strlen counts the letters. Sizeof counts all the bytes. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
